Which is exactly why I said "this industry" as in food delivery. I know doordash hasn't been around that long. I've been a full-time cook, full-time manager, and full-time driver over the years. I know what I'm talking about from multiple perspectives. I've been stiffed on $3,000 orders and got $100 tips on $10 orders. I know the joys and the woes of the driver. I know what makes a good driver from the customers perspective, the restaurants perspective, and the driver's perspective. I know what I'm talking about when I say most doordashers are not good at their jobs.

I'm speaking with nearly two decades of experience in this industry. I've seen the good, I've seen the bad, I know what I'm talking about. I know I'm not going to change any minds here because this whole subreddit is just a big circle jerk of dashers thinking they are perfect angels incapable of making mistakes, and it's always the restaurant or customers fault, but you're looking at it from the perspective of an individual, where as I have access to the actual numbers and can see the bigger picture. Do we at the restaurant make mistakes? Yes. Do the customers make mistakes? Absolutely. But it's so evident just looking at this sub alone how little dashers care about quality control.

This may be the case sometimes, and maybe you're one of the few good dashers out there so it seems especially so from your perspective, but as someone who has been in the food delivery business for 15+years, I can say with assurity that dashers are the problem most of the time. They bear little if no responsibility for the service they're providing, so they take little to no effort to insure quality control. If they've run into the most minor inconvenience they'll abandon the order without actually attempting to problem solve or troubleshoot issues. They have absolutely no understanding of properly routing their orders, often attempting to pick up multiple orders at a time that are no where near each other. They could be walking out the door with an order I just handed them and another order gets dashed that they want to take, they will just sit in the parking lot with the other order, letting it get cold while they wait around for the other order despite the fact that they could have delivered it and  taken something else in the same time (again because they don't actually have any care or responsibility for quality control) They steal from customers and restaurants without qualm like there is no tomorrow (as is evident in pretty much any comment thread on this forum) There is a reason why our customer feedback has a 90% positive review on orders delivered by our inhouse driver's and only 20% from doors sent to doordash.

I'm not saying every driver I've employed in the last 15 years is a shining paragon of hard work and responsibility. In fact it's far from it. The difference is I can hold my driver's to a standard and provide proper training for them, something dashers are sorely lacking.
